svg.title: System lifecycle — the states the whole app shares, and where a user gets stuck
svg.desc: States are combinations of facts, not screens: setup_complete, a rootfs on disk, health, whether the server answers, and who holds the environment lock. Edges are labelled with the guard that allows them, cited to file:line. Red states are dead ends. Read this before drawing any per-area diagram, and reuse these state names verbatim.
svg.text: System lifecycle — where a user gets stuck
A state is a combination of facts, never a screen. Verified against the working tree, 12 Aug. Every edge cites the guard that allows it.

DEAD ENDS, WORST FIRST — traps, then one-way doors, then exits nobody can find, then controls that do nothing
Ranked by how hard the state is to escape, not by how ugly it looks. Only finding 1 survives closing the app — but see its note: the hang is the rarer half of that leg's problem.
Findings 1, 2, 3 and 4 are one sentence four times: a fact nobody clears. They are rows in the standing directive's ledger at the top of operation-model-roadmap.svg — fix them there, not here.
1 · TRAP — a hung install holds the boot gate, and it keeps itself alive (the rarer half; see the note)
Every other gate branch has a safety timer; the installing branch deliberately has none, so the gate lifts only on a terminal install state. InstallService runs in
the foreground, so a run that stops reporting keeps its own process alive and InstallProgressRepository keeps saying "running" — this is the one finding here that
does not clear itself when the app is closed. Force-stop is the only way out, and force-stop does not clear the install marker, so the next launch lands in recovery.
redesign/LibraryActivity.java:277-280, 306-312 (the trade-off is stated), 559-563 (Back → moveTaskToBack) · InstallService.java:221 (startForeground).
Corrected 13 Aug: this is the rarer half. A gate that hangs needs waitFor() never to return; far more often the leg terminates and LIES — see the note below.

Opens with: each leg of the pipeline ending in a terminal that is true, which the module queue already does (:802-826) and the kiwix index (:478-479) and maps (:545-546) do not — they send exit AND error to the next step, so a

failed run reports as a finished install. Not a watchdog on this screen: the truth is at the source. Download → ADFA-4895, maps → ADFA-4898, the rest → ADFA-5119, all under the download contract ADFA-4893.
2 · HIDDEN EXIT — a stale "busy" flag refuses every deep operation, and the way out has no name
A download service killed before reaching a terminal state leaves EnvironmentLock.isBusyNow() true. Clone, backup, restore, module install and the dashboard rebuild
all refuse, all with the same message — "An install is already running" — while nothing is running. It is not durable: every source it reads is in-memory, so closing
the app clears it. That is the whole problem. The exit exists and nobody will find it, because no one closes an app to unblock a button.
env/EnvironmentLock.java:69-87 (all four sources are process-scoped), 97-100 (the file names this and points at ADFA-4874).

Opens with: an age past which a session is ignored, and a message that says what is actually holding the lock. Belongs with ADFA-5106 — the expiry needs the per-session timestamp that ticket produces.
3 · ONE-WAY — the door a user could choose is shut; the one that opens on failure is not
ADFA-5116 removed both Skip buttons and it worked: verified on the updated tree, every wizard path now installs, clones, or returns to the wizard. Download
deliberately does not mark setup complete (ADFA-4982), and Step 1's Back routes through Library, which bounces straight back. Nothing is left to opt out with.
What remains is not a choice, which is why it is harder to see. "Copy from a phone" marks setup complete before any transfer exists, and a first install marks it
when the install STARTS rather than when it succeeds — so a failed install, a failed clone, or a reinstall that destroys the rootfs without finishing all land in
S1. From there the app routes to Library forever and never offers the wizard again, because none of the four writers ever sets the flag false.
Writers: WizardActivity:308 (Copy) · SetupLibraryActivity:284 (install start) · MainActivity:276 · SetupSectionFragment:245. Read at LibraryActivity:84.
Opens with: writing it on a verified install rather than on intent, and clearing it wherever a rootfs is destroyed — the five destructive routes ADFA-5070 hooks.
4 · HIDDEN EXIT — a damaged system reached by the wrong door is never diagnosed
The recovery dialog only runs when the launch takes the "recovering" branch. If a lock is held, or an install or a module queue is running, the branch is skipped and
the user lands on Home — where the install marker forces isSystemInstalled() false, so it presents as "no system": no dialog, no Retry, no mention of damage. The
exits from there are the ones in finding 5, and none of them says anything about a damaged system, so the user is looking for the wrong problem.
LibraryActivity.java:168-177 (the predicate), :187-204 (the redirects that pre-empt it), :287-293 (a held lock lifts the gate) · SystemStateEvaluator:43-45.
Opens with: computing health where it is displayed rather than only in the launch branch. It is already computed app-wide and read by exactly one screen.
5 · HIDDEN EXIT — with no system, the only way forward is a control named "Get more"
The header says "No library yet — tap Get more to install and add content", which is honest, but it is text with no button, on a row deliberately made non-clickable,
pointing at a control at the far bottom of the screen whose name says content rather than system. Meanwhile every card offers Install and Schedule, which route to a
hub that refuses. A user who does not read is offered two wrong doors and one unlabelled right one.
LibraryHomeFragment.java:555, 575, 585-588 (no action on H_NO_LIBRARY) · 244-252 (Get more) · ModuleHubFragment.java:233-243 (the refusal).
6 · DEAD CONTROL — a banked order that is not running is invisible and, for three types, uncancellable
"See progress" appears only while something is actually running, and a refused or deferred drain leaves the order banked without running. Nothing lists it. The module
sheet's Cancel is the only cancel in the app, and it only inspects the maps and module wishlists — a banked ZIM, Books or Courses order cannot be cancelled from
anywhere in the UI.
LibraryHomeFragment.java:518-529 (anyRunning gates the button), :337-342 (isScheduled ignores three of the five wishlists).
7 · DEAD CONTROL — Connect hands out a QR for a box that may not exist
ConnectFragment reads no system fact at all: not isSystemInstalled, not the server state, not the lock. With no system, a damaged one, or the server stopped, the whole
tab behaves normally and prints a QR pointing at a dead port. It is the largest visible-but-useless surface in the app, and the only one that says nothing at all about
why it will not work.
redesign/ConnectFragment.java — browseUrl():126; no reference to SystemFacts, ServerStateRepository or EnvironmentLock anywhere in the file.
